dedupe_keys.name: kakumaaerial aerial imagery benchmark for buildings roof materials toilets and solar panels in kakuma and kalobeyei refugee camps

description: KakumaAerial pairs high-resolution aerial imagery with annotations of buildings and solar panels in the Kakuma and Kalobeyei refugee camps in Turkana County, Kenya. It was published on Zenodo (version 1.0.1, 23 January 2025) by Amrita Gupta, Anthony Ortiz, Simone Fobi, Rahul Dodhia and Juan Lavista Ferres of Microsoft, Duncan Kebut of the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team and Seema Iyer of USA for UNHCR, with a paper for the GeoCV workshop at WACV 2025. Use cases are mapping building and solar panel footprints for planning, population estimation and energy access, classifying roof materials of shelters to judge quality and durability, and identifying toilets to assess sanitation. Files include tiled images (about 17 GB), roof material and toilet classification chips, OpenStreetMap-derived building, toilet and solar annotations from October 2024, background samples and split definitions. Coverage: the two camps. Access: Zenodo, with code on GitHub. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: irregular layouts and mixed materials make detection hard, which the benchmark is designed to test. Simulation uses: shelter inventories for camp planning, hazard exposure and service access. Related records: the Kutupalong settlement evacuation case study.
